s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic skin lesions with possible traumatic onset, localized to the nose
salient_findings: Papules and pustules on the nose
key_facts: 63-year-old patient
1-month history of skin lesions
Lesions located on the nasal dorsum
Erythematous base with multiple papules and pustules
Some lesions with superficial ulceration and yellow crusting
No fever, cough, or joint pain
No hypertension, diabetes, or immunosuppression in medical history
No palpable lymphadenopathy
No improvement with systemic and topical antibiotics

salient_findings: Papules and pustules on the nose
key_facts: 63-year-old patient

Some lesions with superficial ulceration and yellow crusting

differentials: Neutrophilic dermatosis of the dorsal hands
Cutaneous leishmaniasis due to Leishmania braziliensis
per_call: Neutrophilic dermatosis of the dorsal hands

shortlist.label: Lupus miliaris disseminatus faciei
shortlist.why_kept: matches the description of chronic skin lesions with possible traumatic onset, localized to the nose

shortlist.label: Lupus vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with chronic skin lesions and history of trauma, although less common

shortlist.label: Rosacea
shortlist.why_kept: erythematous base with papules and pustules, common condition in this age group

shortlist.label: Granuloma faciale
shortlist.why_kept: matches the description of chronic skin lesions with erythematous base and papules

shortlist.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: possible match given the chronic nature of the lesions and lack of systemic symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple papules and pustules on an erythematous base over the nasal dorsum, with some lesions having superficial ulceration and yellow crusting, is consistent with Lupus miliaris disseminatus faciei, a condition characterized by chronic, recurrent, and inflammatory facial lesions.

rejected.label: Lupus vulgaris
rejected.why: Lupus vulgaris is a form of cutaneous tuberculosis, which typically presents with larger, more destructive lesions and may be accompanied by systemic symptoms, not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Rosacea
rejected.why: Rosacea typically presents with flushing, telangiectasias, and inflammatory papules and pustules, but the presence of superficial ulceration and yellow crusting is not typical for rosacea.

rejected.label: Granuloma faciale
rejected.why: Granuloma faciale is a rare condition characterized by single or multiple, brownish to violaceous, well-circumscribed plaques or nodules on the face, which does not match the patient's presentation of multiple papules and pustules.

rejected.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Discoid lupus erythematosus typically presents with well-defined, disk-shaped, scaly plaques, which may be atrophic, but the patient's lesions are described as papules and pustules on an erythematous base, not matching the typical discoid lupus presentation.
